jobs.title: Global Investigations Manager
jobs.description:
As an Investigation Manager, you will conduct a diverse array of investigative work over whistleblowing allegations including potential improprieties by external parties, such as agents and vendors, and violations of AXA XL’s Code of Conduct and established policies by employees.

You will be responsible for performing an initial assessment of each allegation’s level of severity, creating an investigative plan, interacting with stakeholders (e.g. Compliance, Claims, Human Resource, Legal, Underwriting), gathering evidence, leading sensitive interviews, providing a recommendation on action(s) to be taken, and preparing a report in support of work performed and decisions reached. You will also assist the AXA XL Head of Investigations in preparing activity reports to be shared with executive management and Audit Committee members.

What You’ll Be Doing

What will your essential responsibilities include?

Conducting global internal investigations into violations of AXA XL Corporate policies, regulation or law either self-directed or partnering with cross-functional teams
Developing and executing investigative plans to gather information to assess validity of allegations
Communicating with stakeholders during the investigations, including members of the Compliance, Human Resources and Legal teams, as well as other key stakeholders
Performing complex investigations and monitoring related activities performed by others within AXA XL covering matters across the division involving multicultural teams and stakeholders
Conducting effective interviews at multiple levels of seniority in complex and sometimes sensitive investigations
Collecting and analysing relevant facts and evidence pertaining to the specific case in support of or to refute an allegation
Partnering with Subject Matter Experts, e.g. Compliance, Legal and HR to determine appropriate corrective actions and outcomes. preparing concise and meaningful reports following the completion of investigations and ensuring adherence to all AXA XL Investigations standards. providing timely and meaningful updates pertaining to in-progress and completed investigations and keeping the AXA XL Head of Investigations updated on the status of assigned investigations
Advising concerned parties of outcomes and next steps
Training, coaching, guiding and supervising audit team members assigned to investigations, ensuring work is performed consistently and in accordance with AXA XL Investigations standards
Continuous improvement including reviewing investigations standards and harmonizing with best practices within AXA Group Investigations.

You will report to the AXA XL Head of Investigations. This role may involve international travel (up to 10%), as needed in conjunction with investigative activities, and a flexible work schedule to facilitate interactions with individuals located across the world.

What You Will BRING

We’re looking for someone who has these abilities and skills:

Solid experience with fraud or financial crime investigations, or relevant background in other forensic investigation environment
Experience with High-risk HR Investigations desirable
Legal background desirable but not required
Continuous learning mindset and motivation to furthering your understanding about investigative techniques and insurance industry
Demonstrated expertise in preparing for and conducting investigation interviews
Effective oral and written communication
Outstanding project management, including ability to conduct multiple, concurrent investigations
Sound understanding of current and emerging issues in the financial crime environment
Pragmatic analysis and problem-solving skills
Excellent organizational and time management skills with the ability to prioritize workload
Proven ability to work effectively across a complex matrixed organization
Ability to operate with autonomy and limited supervision
Ability to build robust relationships with colleagues across the organization
Unquestioned integrity and excellent judgement
Demonstrated ability to coach colleagues and provide practical guidance on investigation techniques.

Who WE are

AXA XL, the P&C and specialty risk division of AXA, is known for solving complex risks. For mid-sized companies, multinationals and even some inspirational individuals we don’t just provide re/insurance, we reinvent it.

How? By combining a comprehensive and efficient capital platform, data-driven insights, leading technology, and the best talent in an agile and inclusive workspace, empowered to deliver top client service across all our lines of business − property, casualty, professional, financial lines and specialty.

With an innovative and flexible approach to risk solutions, we partner with those who move the world forward.

Learn more at axaxl.com.

What we OFFER

Inclusion

AXA XL is committed to equal employment opportunity and will consider applicants regardless of gender, sexual orientation, age, ethnicity and origins, marital status, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. At AXA XL, we know that an inclusive culture and enables business growth and is critical to our success. That’s why we have made a strategic commitment to attract, develop, advance and retain the most inclusive workforce possible, and create a culture where everyone can bring their full selves to work and reach their highest potential. It’s about helping one another — and our business — to move forward and succeed.

Five Business Resource Groups focused on gender, LGBTQ+, ethnicity and origins, disability and inclusion with 20 Chapters around the globe.
Robust support for Flexible Working Arrangements
Enhanced family-friendly leave benefits
Named to the Diversity Best Practices Index
Signatory to the UK Women in Finance Charter

Learn more at Inclusion & Diversity at AXA XL | AXA XL. AXA XL is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Total Rewards

AXA XL’s Reward program is designed to take care of what matters most to you, covering the full picture of your health, wellbeing, lifestyle and financial security. It provides enterprising compensation and personalized, inclusive benefits that evolve as you do.

We’re committed to rewarding your contribution for the long term, so you can be your best self today and look forward to the future with confidence.

Sustainability

At AXA XL, Sustainability is integral to our business strategy. In an ever-changing world, AXA XL protects what matters most for our clients and communities. We know that sustainability is at the root of a more resilient future. Our 2023-26 Sustainability strategy, called “Roots of resilience”, focuses on protecting natural ecosystems, addressing climate change, and embedding sustainable practices across our operations.

Our Pillars

Valuing nature: How we impact nature affects how nature impacts us. Resilient ecosystems - the foundation of a sustainable planet and society – are essential to our future. We’re committed to protecting and restoring nature – from mangrove forests to the bees in our backyard – by increasing biodiversity awareness and inspiring clients and colleagues to put nature at the heart of their plans.
Addressing climate change: The effects of a changing climate are far-reaching and significant. Unpredictable weather, increasing temperatures, and rising sea levels cause both social inequalities and environmental disruption. We're building a net zero strategy, developing insurance products and services, and mobilizing to advance thought leadership and investment in societal-led solutions.
Integrating ESG: All companies have a role to play in building a more resilient future. Incorporating ESG considerations into our internal processes and practices builds resilience from the roots of our business. We’re training our colleagues, engaging our external partners, and evolving our sustainability governance and reporting.
AXA Hearts in Action: We have established volunteering and charitable giving programs to help colleagues support causes that matter most to them, known as AXA XL’s “Hearts in Action” programs. These include our Matching Gifts program, Volunteering Leave, and our annual volunteering day – the Global Day of Giving.

For more information, please see Sustainability at AXA XL.

Actual pay will be determined based upon the individual’s skills, experience and location. We strive for market alignment and internal equity with our colleagues’ pay.

We also believe in fostering our colleagues' development and offer a wide range of learning opportunities for colleagues to hone their professional skills and to position themselves for the next step of their careers. jobs.title: All-Source Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Number: R0250810

All-Source Intelligence Analyst

The Opportunity:

With all of the information available today, it takes a skilled all-source analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our government and military every day, we need an intelligence analyst like you to do just that. As a defense industries all-source analyst, you use your specialized functional experience and your attention to detail to conduct all-source analytic production on foreign defense industrial programs, infrastructure, and capabilities supporting a foreign country’s ability to develop, equip, sustain, and employ its military forces across basic, strategic, and military industrial sectors.

As a Defense Industries All-Source Analyst on our team, you’ll help your client by providing intelligence production and briefing support to address dynamic intelligence requirements. Using your comprehensive understanding of all-source analytic tradecraft, production cycles, publication standards, community writing styles, and formats, you’ll produce strategic-level assessments and products that address the research, development, acquisition, test, evaluation and production of foreign weapon systems and equipment. As an authority on your topic, your client will look to you for comprehensive production, often under pressure.

This is a chance to grow your expertise and broaden your skill set in areas like analysis, writing, and communication. You’ll share your expertise with other analysts through leadership and mentoring. We focus on growing as a team to deliver the best support to our customers, so you’ll have resources to learn new skills and tools. Join us as we provide the right information at the right time to support the critical needs of our warfighters and nation’s leaders.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

Knowledge of IC and Combatant Command environments
Ability to develop high-quality deliverables tailored to senior policymakers or defense stakeholders, including complex written products and formal or informal briefings
TS/SCI clearance
Bachelor's degree and 3+ years of experience in all-source analysis, or 7+ years of experience in all-source analysis in lieu of a degree

Nice If You Have:

3+ years of experience with defense industries analysis such as industrial organization, production processes, foreign weapon systems and equipment, and their associated facilities and output levels
Knowledge of ICD 203 and 206 analytic tradecraft standards
Knowledge of the INDOPACOM AOR

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; TS/SCI clearance is required.

Compensation

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $62,000.00 to $141,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date.

Identity Statement

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

Candidate AI Usage Policy

AI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your
own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided
.

Work Model

Our people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.

Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.
Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen or customer facility, in alignment with your leadership's expectations and the needs of the role.
Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed full-time at a customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role.

Commitment to Non-Discrimination

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law.

The Company

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.

At Dexcom, our Global Security team is redefining what it means to protect a mission-driven organization. We are more than a protective layer; we are embedded partners in innovation, culture, and care. We work shoulder-to-shoulder with teams across the company, utilizing secure-by-design principles, enabling innovation, safeguarding trust, and supporting the people who make life-changing technology possible.

This role isn’t just about security, it’s about leadership, partnership, and impact. You’ll join a team that’s building a modern, proactive security program rooted in strategy, prevention, collaboration, and service. We work cross-functionally, think globally, and act locally. If you’re energized by complexity, thrive in dynamic environments, and want to be part of a team that’s as mission driven as the company it protects, come join us!

Where You Come In

You conduct travel risk assessments and threat assessments in support of executive protection operations, senior leader travel, and corporate events.
You support insider threat investigations in coordination with HR, Legal, IT and other stakeholders.
You research and investigate people of interest who may pose threats to executives, employees, or organizational assets.
You produce clear, concise intelligence reports, executive briefings, and incident summaries for leadership.
You leverage open-source, commercial, and other databases for intelligence collection, trend analysis, and risk forecasting.
You collaborate with the global security operations center on real-time incident monitoring, alerts, and escalations.

You provide intelligence support to Regional Security Managers in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC, tailoring analysis to regional risk profiles and operational needs.
You maintain intelligence databases, case files, and records in accordance with legal, regulatory, and privacy requirements.
You contribute to the continuous improvement of intelligence tradecraft, SOPs, and analytic methodologies.
You support the organization’s executive protection program, special events, and global operations by producing actionable intelligence and risk assessments.
You are responsible for conducting travel, threat and location risk assessments, investigating people of interest, and supporting insider threat investigations led by key stakeholders.
You collaborate closely with the global security operations center during real-time and ongoing incidents.
You also provide support to the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regional security managers, ensuring a coordinated global approach to threat monitoring and mitigation.

What Makes You Successful

You must have 2-4 years of experience in intelligence analysis, protective intelligence, and threat investigations, 2 of which are in a corporate or government environment.
You must have demonstrated experience conducting travel risk assessments, threat investigations, and protective intelligence.
You must have strong analytic, writing, and briefing skills with the ability to distill complex information for executive audiences.
You must have familiarity with intelligence platforms, investigative databases, social media and open-source monitoring tools.
You must have the ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities, with tight deadlines.
You must be collaborative, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work with cross-functional partners.
You should have experience supporting global or multinational operations.
You should have professional certifications (e.g., CTIA, IFCP, etc.) or other intelligence/security credentials from an accredited organization.
You should be an active member of relevant intelligence and security communities (e.g., ASIS, ATAP, etc.) to stay current on best practices, emerging threats, and industry standards.

We're Hiring a Semiconductor Research Analyst

We're looking for an analyst to join our research team covering the semiconductor supply chain — process technology, equipment & materials, advanced packaging, and the Foundry/IDM/Fabless landscape. This role suits someone who enjoys not just deep research, but also presenting insights and working directly with clients.

What you'll do

Track semiconductor industry intelligence — process technology shifts, capacity and pricing dynamics, and supply chain movements as they happen
Present findings directly to clients and prospects, translating data into actionable takeaways
Build and maintain relationships with institutional clients, and play an active role in growing the business

What we're looking for (must-have)

Solid understanding of the semiconductor supply chain
Direct exposure to semiconductor process technology, equipment & materials, advanced packaging, or the Foundry/IDM/Fabless market — via the supply chain or the equity market
Sharp logical and analytical thinking, with the ability to draw valid conclusions from complex data
Strong presentation and communication skills, with a client-service mindset
Fully fluent in English, spoken and written
Strong proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel (charting, graphing, data analysis)

The Threat Operations Analyst supports the daily operation of Internova's end user facing security controls and contributes to the identification, analysis, and disposition of threats affecting the enterprise. The role combines hands on operational work, including end user support, SOC escalation handling, and email and endpoint protection administration, with analytical work covering event triage, phishing and business email compromise analysis, threat intelligence and brand protection monitoring of Internova's external footprint, and validation of vulnerabilities and reported threats.

The Internova Travel Group Information Security Team is committed to providing outstanding support to our team members to ensure continued growth opportunities, and access to extraordinary tools and technology. Our corporate culture encourages leaders at all levels to think independently, make decisions autonomously, and inspire passion in all aspects of our work.

Address end user support request for information security issues and SOC escalation requests.
Day to day administration of end user facing security technologies (Mimecast, Microsoft 365 ATP, Cisco Umbrella, Cisco AMP)
Monitor and report on security events across multiple internal platforms, performing first line triage and escalating with sufficient documentation for downstream analysis.
Support phishing and business email compromise defense, including analysis of user reported messages, tuning of ATP and Mimecast rule sets, and extraction of indicators for blocking and detection use.
Track threat activity relevant to the travel and hospitality sector using Recorded Future and other sources, including business email compromise, credential stuffing, booking and payment fraud, and supplier impersonation, and summarize the impact for Internova.
Day to day use of Recorded Future for threat intelligence and brand reputation monitoring, including alert triage, watch list and query maintenance, indicator enrichment, and routing of actionable intelligence to the appropriate owner.
Investigate brand and domain impersonation, typosquatting, exposed services, and credential exposure affecting Internova and its brands, coordinating takedown and blocking action and reporting findings to enterprise security leadership.
Supplement platform reporting with independent open source intelligence collection, structuring findings so they can be acted on rather than simply forwarded.
Validate and triage vulnerability scanner and security tooling output, separating exploitable findings from false positives and tracking remediation to closure with application and infrastructure owners.
Assist information security team members with project tasks, troubleshooting, and administration responsibilities, and recommend tooling and process enhancements to senior information security staff.

0 to two years of professional experience, inclusive of internships, co-ops, or research appointments in security operations, threat analysis, penetration testing, or application security.

Working knowledge of common attack techniques against web applications, APIs, identity systems, and email, including authentication, authorization, injection, and business logic flaws.
Understanding of indicators of compromise and how they are collected, enriched, and applied to detection and blocking.
Exposure to at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and to core cloud security concepts such as identity, logging, and network segmentation.
Familiarity with industry standard encryption technologies and cybersecurity technical controls.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risk to non technical stakeholders and to write findings a reader can act on.

jobs.title: Security Risk Analyst, Risk Engineering
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

The Security Risk team is responsible for how Anthropic identifies, prioritizes, and drives treatment of its most important security risks. We are rebuilding risk management to operate as an engineering function, using automation, quantitative risk and AI-native platforms to enable decision making. The risks we assess span Anthropic's full security landscape, so the team needs breadth across domains and the judgment to go deep wherever a decision demands it. Security Risk, in deep partnership with Security Engineering, helps define the security program and shapes how investment and treatment decisions get made.

The conventional GRC playbook was not built for a company shipping frontier AI. You will help define what replaces it, with a direct line to CISO-level decisions. As a Security Risk Analyst you will take risk questions from leadership and partner teams and drive them to a decision. Sometimes that is a fast, structured qualitative assessment and other times it is a deep FAIR-based quantitative analysis. Either way you bring leadership a clear position, the tradeoffs, and honest uncertainty, and you defend it under challenge. In parallel, you will help turn quantitative risk into a product partner teams can leverage, and define the standards a growing risk function will run on.

Key Responsibilities

Enable leadership and partner teams to make risk-informed decisions. Take ambiguous risk questions, drive them to a documented decision, and communicate the quantitative and qualitative tradeoffs clearly
Lead quantitative analysis of the company's top security risk scenarios using FAIR, calibrated estimation, and simulation, working with the engineers who own the systems and presenting results in terms leadership can act on
Partner with Security Engineering to assess threat scenarios and control effectiveness so security investment is right-sized to actual risk and remediation is sequenced where it buys down the most risk
Frame escalations and risk treatment decisions with a clear recommendation, an honest statement of uncertainty, and re-evaluation triggers, and pressure test those decisions with risk owners
Shape the analysis and narrative behind leadership risk reviews, and help define risk appetite and the risk metrics the organization should measure and why
Use AI and automation to scale risk analysis, and own the calibration and quality review that keep the outputs trustworthy
Turn one-off analyses into reusable methods, templates, and training so risk analysis becomes increasingly self service for partner teams, and raise the analytical quality of the risk register

You may be a good fit if you

Have owned security or technology risk analysis end to end, qualitative and quantitative, and can point to a decision your output changed, whether a funding call, a launch call, a remediation sequence, or a documented acceptance
Have hands-on FAIR-style quantification experience, including scenario decomposition, calibrated estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation in Python, R, or spreadsheet tooling, briefed to decision makers
Thrive in ambiguity. You frame a moving question into something analyzable, pick the depth that fits, and drive to a decision rather than a report
Put defensible severity and likelihood on ambiguous problems, state uncertainty honestly, and change your position when the evidence changes
Have enough technical security depth to decompose an attack path with security engineers and be credible in the room
Can compress a complex risk position into one paragraph for the CISO, make the tradeoff explicit, and defend it under pointed questions
Use Claude or other LLMs as daily working tools and review model output critically
Are low ego and collaborative, build credibility through the work, and care about AI safety and the role security risk plays in it

Strong candidates may also

Have applied FAIR-CAM or another structured approach to control effectiveness and attack path modeling
Have built or operated a cyber risk quantification program, or turned quantitative analysis into tooling, templates, or training that others ran
Have helped define risk appetite or tolerance thresholds an organization actually used to make decisions
Bring a background in security engineering, detection, threat intelligence, actuarial science, or decision science that grounds the numbers in real systems
Are familiar with security risks specific to AI systems, such as goal or intent modification, and how they change traditional threat models

jobs.title: Security Risk Analyst, Risk Engineering
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

The Security Risk team is responsible for how Anthropic identifies, prioritizes, and drives treatment of its most important security risks. We are rebuilding risk management to operate as an engineering function, using automation, quantitative risk and AI-native platforms to enable decision making. The risks we assess span Anthropic's full security landscape, so the team needs breadth across domains and the judgment to go deep wherever a decision demands it. Security Risk, in deep partnership with Security Engineering, helps define the security program and shapes how investment and treatment decisions get made.

The conventional GRC playbook was not built for a company shipping frontier AI. You will help define what replaces it, with a direct line to CISO-level decisions. As a Security Risk Analyst you will take risk questions from leadership and partner teams and drive them to a decision. Sometimes that is a fast, structured qualitative assessment and other times it is a deep FAIR-based quantitative analysis. Either way you bring leadership a clear position, the tradeoffs, and honest uncertainty, and you defend it under challenge. In parallel, you will help turn quantitative risk into a product partner teams can leverage, and define the standards a growing risk function will run on.

Key Responsibilities

Enable leadership and partner teams to make risk-informed decisions. Take ambiguous risk questions, drive them to a documented decision, and communicate the quantitative and qualitative tradeoffs clearly
Lead quantitative analysis of the company's top security risk scenarios using FAIR, calibrated estimation, and simulation, working with the engineers who own the systems and presenting results in terms leadership can act on
Partner with Security Engineering to assess threat scenarios and control effectiveness so security investment is right-sized to actual risk and remediation is sequenced where it buys down the most risk
Frame escalations and risk treatment decisions with a clear recommendation, an honest statement of uncertainty, and re-evaluation triggers, and pressure test those decisions with risk owners
Shape the analysis and narrative behind leadership risk reviews, and help define risk appetite and the risk metrics the organization should measure and why
Use AI and automation to scale risk analysis, and own the calibration and quality review that keep the outputs trustworthy
Turn one-off analyses into reusable methods, templates, and training so risk analysis becomes increasingly self service for partner teams, and raise the analytical quality of the risk register

You may be a good fit if you

Have owned security or technology risk analysis end to end, qualitative and quantitative, and can point to a decision your output changed, whether a funding call, a launch call, a remediation sequence, or a documented acceptance
Have hands-on FAIR-style quantification experience, including scenario decomposition, calibrated estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation in Python, R, or spreadsheet tooling, briefed to decision makers
Thrive in ambiguity. You frame a moving question into something analyzable, pick the depth that fits, and drive to a decision rather than a report
Put defensible severity and likelihood on ambiguous problems, state uncertainty honestly, and change your position when the evidence changes
Have enough technical security depth to decompose an attack path with security engineers and be credible in the room
Can compress a complex risk position into one paragraph for the CISO, make the tradeoff explicit, and defend it under pointed questions
Use Claude or other LLMs as daily working tools and review model output critically
Are low ego and collaborative, build credibility through the work, and care about AI safety and the role security risk plays in it

Strong candidates may also

Have applied FAIR-CAM or another structured approach to control effectiveness and attack path modeling
Have built or operated a cyber risk quantification program, or turned quantitative analysis into tooling, templates, or training that others ran
Have helped define risk appetite or tolerance thresholds an organization actually used to make decisions
Bring a background in security engineering, detection, threat intelligence, actuarial science, or decision science that grounds the numbers in real systems
Are familiar with security risks specific to AI systems, such as goal or intent modification, and how they change traditional threat models

jobs.title: Global Investigations Manager
jobs.description:
As an Investigation Manager, you will conduct a diverse array of investigative work over whistleblowing allegations including potential improprieties by external parties, such as agents and vendors, and violations of AXA XL’s Code of Conduct and established policies by employees.

You will be responsible for performing an initial assessment of each allegation’s level of severity, creating an investigative plan, interacting with stakeholders (e.g. Compliance, Claims, Human Resource, Legal, Underwriting), gathering evidence, leading sensitive interviews, providing a recommendation on action(s) to be taken, and preparing a report in support of work performed and decisions reached. You will also assist the AXA XL Head of Investigations in preparing activity reports to be shared with executive management and Audit Committee members.

What You’ll Be Doing

What will your essential responsibilities include?

Conducting global internal investigations into violations of AXA XL Corporate policies, regulation or law either self-directed or partnering with cross-functional teams
Developing and executing investigative plans to gather information to assess validity of allegations
Communicating with stakeholders during the investigations, including members of the Compliance, Human Resources and Legal teams, as well as other key stakeholders
Performing complex investigations and monitoring related activities performed by others within AXA XL covering matters across the division involving multicultural teams and stakeholders
Conducting effective interviews at multiple levels of seniority in complex and sometimes sensitive investigations
Collecting and analysing relevant facts and evidence pertaining to the specific case in support of or to refute an allegation
Partnering with Subject Matter Experts, e.g. Compliance, Legal and HR to determine appropriate corrective actions and outcomes. preparing concise and meaningful reports following the completion of investigations and ensuring adherence to all AXA XL Investigations standards. providing timely and meaningful updates pertaining to in-progress and completed investigations and keeping the AXA XL Head of Investigations updated on the status of assigned investigations
Advising concerned parties of outcomes and next steps
Training, coaching, guiding and supervising audit team members assigned to investigations, ensuring work is performed consistently and in accordance with AXA XL Investigations standards
Continuous improvement including reviewing investigations standards and harmonizing with best practices within AXA Group Investigations.

You will report to the AXA XL Head of Investigations. This role may involve international travel (up to 10%), as needed in conjunction with investigative activities, and a flexible work schedule to facilitate interactions with individuals located across the world.

What You Will BRING

We’re looking for someone who has these abilities and skills:

Solid experience with fraud or financial crime investigations, or relevant background in other forensic investigation environment
Experience with High-risk HR Investigations desirable
Legal background desirable but not required
Continuous learning mindset and motivation to furthering your understanding about investigative techniques and insurance industry
Demonstrated expertise in preparing for and conducting investigation interviews
Effective oral and written communication
Outstanding project management, including ability to conduct multiple, concurrent investigations
Sound understanding of current and emerging issues in the financial crime environment
Pragmatic analysis and problem-solving skills
Excellent organizational and time management skills with the ability to prioritize workload
Proven ability to work effectively across a complex matrixed organization
Ability to operate with autonomy and limited supervision
Ability to build robust relationships with colleagues across the organization
Unquestioned integrity and excellent judgement
Demonstrated ability to coach colleagues and provide practical guidance on investigation techniques.

Who WE are

AXA XL, the P&C and specialty risk division of AXA, is known for solving complex risks. For mid-sized companies, multinationals and even some inspirational individuals we don’t just provide re/insurance, we reinvent it.

How? By combining a comprehensive and efficient capital platform, data-driven insights, leading technology, and the best talent in an agile and inclusive workspace, empowered to deliver top client service across all our lines of business − property, casualty, professional, financial lines and specialty.

With an innovative and flexible approach to risk solutions, we partner with those who move the world forward.

Learn more at axaxl.com.

What we OFFER

Inclusion

AXA XL is committed to equal employment opportunity and will consider applicants regardless of gender, sexual orientation, age, ethnicity and origins, marital status, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. At AXA XL, we know that an inclusive culture and enables business growth and is critical to our success. That’s why we have made a strategic commitment to attract, develop, advance and retain the most inclusive workforce possible, and create a culture where everyone can bring their full selves to work and reach their highest potential. It’s about helping one another — and our business — to move forward and succeed.

Five Business Resource Groups focused on gender, LGBTQ+, ethnicity and origins, disability and inclusion with 20 Chapters around the globe.
Robust support for Flexible Working Arrangements
Enhanced family-friendly leave benefits
Named to the Diversity Best Practices Index
Signatory to the UK Women in Finance Charter

Learn more at Inclusion & Diversity at AXA XL | AXA XL. AXA XL is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Total Rewards

AXA XL’s Reward program is designed to take care of what matters most to you, covering the full picture of your health, wellbeing, lifestyle and financial security. It provides enterprising compensation and personalized, inclusive benefits that evolve as you do.

We’re committed to rewarding your contribution for the long term, so you can be your best self today and look forward to the future with confidence.

Sustainability

At AXA XL, Sustainability is integral to our business strategy. In an ever-changing world, AXA XL protects what matters most for our clients and communities. We know that sustainability is at the root of a more resilient future. Our 2023-26 Sustainability strategy, called “Roots of resilience”, focuses on protecting natural ecosystems, addressing climate change, and embedding sustainable practices across our operations.

Our Pillars

Valuing nature: How we impact nature affects how nature impacts us. Resilient ecosystems - the foundation of a sustainable planet and society – are essential to our future. We’re committed to protecting and restoring nature – from mangrove forests to the bees in our backyard – by increasing biodiversity awareness and inspiring clients and colleagues to put nature at the heart of their plans.
Addressing climate change: The effects of a changing climate are far-reaching and significant. Unpredictable weather, increasing temperatures, and rising sea levels cause both social inequalities and environmental disruption. We're building a net zero strategy, developing insurance products and services, and mobilizing to advance thought leadership and investment in societal-led solutions.
Integrating ESG: All companies have a role to play in building a more resilient future. Incorporating ESG considerations into our internal processes and practices builds resilience from the roots of our business. We’re training our colleagues, engaging our external partners, and evolving our sustainability governance and reporting.
AXA Hearts in Action: We have established volunteering and charitable giving programs to help colleagues support causes that matter most to them, known as AXA XL’s “Hearts in Action” programs. These include our Matching Gifts program, Volunteering Leave, and our annual volunteering day – the Global Day of Giving.

For more information, please see Sustainability at AXA XL.

Do you have strong technical skills in research and data analysis? Are you interested in making a meaningful impact on the lives children and families across California? If so, consider joining the Fiscal Forecasting Branch (FFB) at the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) as a Research Data Analyst (RDA) II, also considering RDA I. This position is part of a dynamic team that is dedicated to serving, aiding and protecting children and adults in ways that strengthen and preserve families, encourage personal responsibility and foster independence. We are looking for a highly motivated Research Data Analyst I/II (RDA I/II) with strong analytical skills who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment to join the Children’s Estimates Unit of the Fiscal Forecasting Branch (FFB) team. The Children’s Estimates Unit develops the annual Local Assistance Governor’s Budget and May Revision update for Children’s programs administered by the County Welfare Departments. In addition, the FFB is responsible for providing a fiscal analysis of proposed legislative bills that have a potential impact to the Department.

The RDA II’s serve as a senior analysts that working with minimal direction, while the RDA I supports complex analysis under general direction. jobs.description:
Job Description

The Program Manager, Quality Assurance, is responsible for leading and overseeing quality assurance operations related to outpatient Substance Use Disorder (SUD) treatment programs regulated by the Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC). This position manages a team of Audit Coordinators responsible for conducting compliance audits, monitoring departmental performance, and ensuring adherence to federal, state, contractual, and HHSC requirements.

The Program Manager provides strategic direction, supervision, and technical guidance to audit staff; develops and implements quality assurance initiatives; analyzes audit findings and trends; and collaborates with program leadership to drive continuous quality improvement. The position serves as a subject matter expert on regulatory compliance and performance monitoring, ensuring that outpatient SUD programs maintain high standards of service delivery and regulatory compliance.

Key responsibilities include overseeing audit planning and execution, reviewing audit results and performance improvement plans, identifying systemic compliance risks, developing policies and procedures, monitoring quality metrics, and preparing reports and presentations for executive leadership and regulatory agencies. The Program Manager fosters a culture of accountability, compliance, and continuous improvement while supporting organizational goals and ensuring readiness for HHSC audits, reviews, and inspections.

This position requires strong leadership, analytical, and communication skills, as well as extensive knowledge of behavioral health regulations, quality management principles, and auditing practices related to outpatient SUD treatment services.

Responsibilities

Manage the planning, scheduling, and conducting of full‑scope and targeted audits of SUD and related programs to verify compliance with HHSC regulations, contractual SOWs, and TAC requirements.
Validate service delivery against contractually required service levels, client/participant satisfaction, service capacity, access to services, populations served, evidence‑based practices, and timeframes.
Manage auditors to ensure the completeness of on‑site visits across Texas to observe operations, perform data integrity checks across EHR/EMR systems, conduct facility walkthroughs, and evaluate environment of care.
Oversee the production of clear, timely audit reports detailing scope, findings, ratings, and risk prioritization.
Collaborate with providers to oversee the development of Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs).
Present audit findings to providers, leadership, and network provider partners.
Partner with provider network to align on standards and remediation.
Lead, mentor, and develop team of auditors by providing technical oversight, facilitating knowledge transfer, and promoting consistent application of audit standards and regulatory requirements.
Perform all other duties as assigned.

The position may require travel within the state of Texas.

Qualifications

Education: Bachelors degree; experience may be substituted in lieu of degree.

Preferred Experience: Experience working within Quality Assurance and auditing. Relevant experience and knowledge working with substance use care and mental health support.

Regulatory Acumen: Interprets and operationalizes HHSC requirements, SOWs, and TAC standards.
Audit Rigor: Applies structured methodologies, risk‑based sampling, and objective scoring.
Data‑Driven: Converts metrics into insights; monitors PIP effectiveness.
Communication & Influence: Writes crisp reports; presents to diverse audiences; builds provider buy‑in.
Field Readiness: Manages extensive travel; adapts to varied provider settings statewide.
Integrity & Judgment: Handles sensitive information; exercises impartial, evidence‑based decision‑making.
Continuous Improvement: Identifies system gaps; recommends pragmatic, sustainable fixes.

Required Skills

Five (5) years of progressively responsible experience is required.

As the third-largest research university in Texas and a Carnegie R1-designated institution, UT San Antonio is a model of access and excellence — advancing knowledge, social mobility and public health across South Texas and beyond. UT San Antonio serves approximately 42,000 students in 320 academic programs spanning science, engineering, medicine, health, liberal arts, AI, cybersecurity, business, education and more. With 17,000 faculty and staff, UT San Antonio has been recognized by Forbes as one of America’s Best Employers for Company Culture .

jobs.description:
About Hytech

Hytech is a leading management consulting firm headquartered in Australia and Singapore, specialising in digital transformation for fintech and financial services organisations. We deliver end-to-end consulting services and provide robust middle- and back-office solutions that enable our clients to optimise operations, enhance efficiency, and stay ahead in a fast-evolving digital landscape. Our client portfolio includes top global trading platforms and leading crypto exchanges.

With more than 2,000 professionals worldwide, Hytech has a strong and growing international presence, with offices across Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, Taiwan, the Philippines, Thailand, Morocco, Cyprus, Dubai, and beyond.

Position Overview

We are seeking a skilled and analytically-minded Data Analyst to strengthen our Group Internal Audit function. This role combines technical data expertise with audit acumen to transform complex datasets into actionable insights that drive more effective and efficient audits across the organization.
You will work at the intersection of data science and internal audit, designing data-driven audit procedures, building analytics frameworks, and presenting compelling visualizations to senior leadership. This is a high-impact position that influences audit strategy and control recommendations across the entire group.

Key Responsibilities

Audit Analytics & Data-Driven Procedures (40%)

Extract, clean, and analyze data from multiple sources (ERP systems, databases, data warehouses) to support audit planning and fieldwork.
Design and execute statistical audit procedures including sampling, anomaly detection, and trend analysis to test control effectiveness.
Develop data-driven audit programs that identify high-risk transactions, unusual patterns, and control exceptions.
Perform forensic-style analysis to investigate control failures and potential fraud indicators.

Data Visualization & Reporting (30%)

Create interactive dashboards and compelling visualizations to communicate audit findings to senior management and audit committees.
Build audit metrics dashboards for real-time monitoring of key control indicators and audit progress.
Translate complex data analyses into clear, business-focused narratives and executive presentations.
Maintain detailed documentation of audit analytics methodologies to support audit trail requirements.

Analytics Automation & Process Improvement (20%)

Identify opportunities to automate routine audit procedures through analytics tools and scripts.
Develop repeatable audit templates and workflows to improve team efficiency and consistency.
Build audit data models and maintain reusable analytics frameworks across audit engagements.
Recommend enhancements to audit scopes based on data patterns and emerging risks.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Support (10%)

Partner with business unit leaders to understand data requirements, control environments, and audit scope.
Collaborate with IT and Finance teams to ensure data access, accuracy, and system integration.
Mentor junior audit staff on data analytics techniques and best practices.
Present findings and recommendations to audit committee members and senior leadership.

Job Requirements

Education & Credentials

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Accounting, Finance, Computer Science, or related field.
Professional certifications preferred: CIA (Certified Internal Auditor), CPA, ACCA, or data analytics certifications (Tableau, Microsoft Certified Data Analyst).
Demonstrated commitment to professional development in audit and analytics.

Experience

Mid-Junior Level:
2-4 years of experience in data analysis, business analysis, internal audit, or financial reporting roles.
Senior Level:
5+ years of progressive experience in audit analytics, internal audit, or enterprise data analytics with track record of designing analytics frameworks and leading audit projects.
Hands-on experience executing data-driven audit procedures; familiarity with audit standards (IIA, COSO, SOX) is valued.
Exposure to ERP systems (SAP, Oracle) and accounting system architecture is an advantage.
Fraud investigation or forensic analysis experience is highly regarded.

Technical & Analytical Skills

Advanced SQL & Programming:
Proficiency in SQL, Python, or R with ability to write complex queries and perform statistical analysis.
Data Visualization:
Hands-on expertise in Tableau, Power BI, or similar tools; proven ability to design effective dashboards.
Audit Analytics Tools:
Experience with ACL, IDEA, or similar audit analytics software is essential.
Excel Mastery:
Advanced functions including pivot tables, VLOOKUP, data modeling, and automation.
Statistical Knowledge:
Sound understanding of descriptive/inferential statistics, sampling methods, hypothesis testing, and anomaly detection.

Soft Skills & Mindset

Strong analytical and critical thinking ability with a skeptical, audit-focused mindset.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to present technical insights to non-technical audiences.
Detail-oriented with unwavering commitment to data accuracy and audit quality.
Collaborative team player who builds effective working relationships across functions.
Proactive problem-solver with drive to continuously improve processes and methodologies.
Self-directed learner eager to stay current with emerging technologies and audit best practices.
Maintains independence, objectivity, and integrity in all audit activities.

Exposure to diverse business functions and operating environments across the group.

Sponsorship for professional certifications (CIA, CPA, data analytics credentials).
Access to latest analytics tools and technologies.

Competitive compensation package aligned with experience level and market benchmarks.

As an Investigation Manager, you will conduct a diverse array of investigative work over whistleblowing allegations including potential improprieties by external parties, such as agents and vendors, and violations of AXA XL’s Code of Conduct and established policies by employees.

You will be responsible for performing an initial assessment of each allegation’s level of severity, creating an investigative plan, interacting with stakeholders (e.g. Compliance, Claims, Human Resource, Legal, Underwriting), gathering evidence, leading sensitive interviews, providing a recommendation on action(s) to be taken, and preparing a report in support of work performed and decisions reached. You will also assist the AXA XL Head of Investigations in preparing activity reports to be shared with executive management and Audit Committee members.

What You’ll Be Doing

What will your essential responsibilities include?

Conducting global internal investigations into violations of AXA XL Corporate policies, regulation or law either self-directed or partnering with cross-functional teams
Developing and executing investigative plans to gather information to assess validity of allegations
Communicating with stakeholders during the investigations, including members of the Compliance, Human Resources and Legal teams, as well as other key stakeholders
Performing complex investigations and monitoring related activities performed by others within AXA XL covering matters across the division involving multicultural teams and stakeholders
Conducting effective interviews at multiple levels of seniority in complex and sometimes sensitive investigations
Collecting and analysing relevant facts and evidence pertaining to the specific case in support of or to refute an allegation
Partnering with Subject Matter Experts, e.g. Compliance, Legal and HR to determine appropriate corrective actions and outcomes. preparing concise and meaningful reports following the completion of investigations and ensuring adherence to all AXA XL Investigations standards. providing timely and meaningful updates pertaining to in-progress and completed investigations and keeping the AXA XL Head of Investigations updated on the status of assigned investigations
Advising concerned parties of outcomes and next steps
Training, coaching, guiding and supervising audit team members assigned to investigations, ensuring work is performed consistently and in accordance with AXA XL Investigations standards
Continuous improvement including reviewing investigations standards and harmonizing with best practices within AXA Group Investigations.

You will report to the AXA XL Head of Investigations. This role may involve international travel (up to 10%), as needed in conjunction with investigative activities, and a flexible work schedule to facilitate interactions with individuals located across the world.

What You Will BRING

We’re looking for someone who has these abilities and skills:

Solid experience with fraud or financial crime investigations, or relevant background in other forensic investigation environment
Experience with High-risk HR Investigations desirable
Legal background desirable but not required
Continuous learning mindset and motivation to furthering your understanding about investigative techniques and insurance industry
Demonstrated expertise in preparing for and conducting investigation interviews
Effective oral and written communication
Outstanding project management, including ability to conduct multiple, concurrent investigations
Sound understanding of current and emerging issues in the financial crime environment
Pragmatic analysis and problem-solving skills
Excellent organizational and time management skills with the ability to prioritize workload
Proven ability to work effectively across a complex matrixed organization
Ability to operate with autonomy and limited supervision
Ability to build robust relationships with colleagues across the organization
Unquestioned integrity and excellent judgement
Demonstrated ability to coach colleagues and provide practical guidance on investigation techniques.

Who WE are

AXA XL, the P&C and specialty risk division of AXA, is known for solving complex risks. For mid-sized companies, multinationals and even some inspirational individuals we don’t just provide re/insurance, we reinvent it.

How? By combining a comprehensive and efficient capital platform, data-driven insights, leading technology, and the best talent in an agile and inclusive workspace, empowered to deliver top client service across all our lines of business − property, casualty, professional, financial lines and specialty.

With an innovative and flexible approach to risk solutions, we partner with those who move the world forward.

Learn more at axaxl.com.

What we OFFER

Inclusion

AXA XL is committed to equal employment opportunity and will consider applicants regardless of gender, sexual orientation, age, ethnicity and origins, marital status, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. At AXA XL, we know that an inclusive culture and enables business growth and is critical to our success. That’s why we have made a strategic commitment to attract, develop, advance and retain the most inclusive workforce possible, and create a culture where everyone can bring their full selves to work and reach their highest potential. It’s about helping one another — and our business — to move forward and succeed.

Five Business Resource Groups focused on gender, LGBTQ+, ethnicity and origins, disability and inclusion with 20 Chapters around the globe.
Robust support for Flexible Working Arrangements
Enhanced family-friendly leave benefits
Named to the Diversity Best Practices Index
Signatory to the UK Women in Finance Charter

Learn more at Inclusion & Diversity at AXA XL | AXA XL. AXA XL is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Total Rewards

AXA XL’s Reward program is designed to take care of what matters most to you, covering the full picture of your health, wellbeing, lifestyle and financial security. It provides enterprising compensation and personalized, inclusive benefits that evolve as you do.

We’re committed to rewarding your contribution for the long term, so you can be your best self today and look forward to the future with confidence.

Sustainability

At AXA XL, Sustainability is integral to our business strategy. In an ever-changing world, AXA XL protects what matters most for our clients and communities. We know that sustainability is at the root of a more resilient future. Our 2023-26 Sustainability strategy, called “Roots of resilience”, focuses on protecting natural ecosystems, addressing climate change, and embedding sustainable practices across our operations.

Our Pillars

Valuing nature: How we impact nature affects how nature impacts us. Resilient ecosystems - the foundation of a sustainable planet and society – are essential to our future. We’re committed to protecting and restoring nature – from mangrove forests to the bees in our backyard – by increasing biodiversity awareness and inspiring clients and colleagues to put nature at the heart of their plans.

jobs.description:
As an Investigation Manager, you will conduct a diverse array of investigative work over whistleblowing allegations including potential improprieties by external parties, such as agents and vendors, and violations of AXA XL’s Code of Conduct and established policies by employees.

You will be responsible for performing an initial assessment of each allegation’s level of severity, creating an investigative plan, interacting with stakeholders (e.g. Compliance, Claims, Human Resource, Legal, Underwriting), gathering evidence, leading sensitive interviews, providing a recommendation on action(s) to be taken, and preparing a report in support of work performed and decisions reached. You will also assist the AXA XL Head of Investigations in preparing activity reports to be shared with executive management and Audit Committee members.

What You’ll Be Doing

What will your essential responsibilities include?

Conducting global internal investigations into violations of AXA XL Corporate policies, regulation or law either self-directed or partnering with cross-functional teams
Developing and executing investigative plans to gather information to assess validity of allegations
Communicating with stakeholders during the investigations, including members of the Compliance, Human Resources and Legal teams, as well as other key stakeholders
Performing complex investigations and monitoring related activities performed by others within AXA XL covering matters across the division involving multicultural teams and stakeholders
Conducting effective interviews at multiple levels of seniority in complex and sometimes sensitive investigations
Collecting and analysing relevant facts and evidence pertaining to the specific case in support of or to refute an allegation
Partnering with Subject Matter Experts, e.g. Compliance, Legal and HR to determine appropriate corrective actions and outcomes. preparing concise and meaningful reports following the completion of investigations and ensuring adherence to all AXA XL Investigations standards. providing timely and meaningful updates pertaining to in-progress and completed investigations and keeping the AXA XL Head of Investigations updated on the status of assigned investigations
Advising concerned parties of outcomes and next steps
Training, coaching, guiding and supervising audit team members assigned to investigations, ensuring work is performed consistently and in accordance with AXA XL Investigations standards
Continuous improvement including reviewing investigations standards and harmonizing with best practices within AXA Group Investigations.

You will report to the AXA XL Head of Investigations. This role may involve international travel (up to 10%), as needed in conjunction with investigative activities, and a flexible work schedule to facilitate interactions with individuals located across the world.

Experience with High-risk HR Investigations desirable

Demonstrated expertise in preparing for and conducting investigation interviews

Description

Summary:

The Senior Project Manager - Payments will have deep domain expertise in payments to join our growing Payments team. In this role, you will own the end-to-end delivery of complex, cross-functional payments initiatives. You will serve as the connective tissue between product, technology, operations, risk, legal, and external partners, ensuring programs are delivered on time, within scope, and with measurable business impact.

The ideal candidate brings a rare combination of rigorous project management methodology and hands-on payments knowledge — someone who can speak fluently about Payment networks in the same conversation as they manage a critical path schedule or escalate a risk to leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Program & Project Delivery

Lead end-to-end delivery of strategic payments programs, including product launches, platform migrations, FinTech integrations, and regulatory compliance initiatives.
Develop and maintain comprehensive project plans, RAID logs (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies), and status dashboards for executive and working-group audiences.
Drive project execution through structured agile/hybrid delivery frameworks, adapting methodology to fit the complexity and compliance requirements of payments projects.
Manage project budgets, resource planning, and vendor contracts in collaboration with Finance and Procurement.
Proactively identify schedule risks and develop mitigation strategies; escalate blockers with clear recommended paths to resolution.

Payments Domain Leadership

Apply deep knowledge of the payments ecosystem to shape project scope, anticipate integration challenges, and guide technical teams through payments-specific complexity.
Serve as the internal subject matter authority on payment rails and schemes including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, NACHA/ACH, RTP, FedNow, SWIFT, and emerging real-time networks.
Partner with Product and Technology to define acceptance criteria for payment flows, ensuring compliance with network rules, regulatory requirements (PCI-DSS, Reg E, PSD2, NACHA Operating Rules), and security standards.
Champion best practices in payments security, fraud mitigation, tokenization, and authentication (3DS, biometrics) throughout the project lifecycle.

Stakeholder Management & Communication

Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders across Product, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Finance, and external partners.
Facilitate and lead cross-functional steering committees, working groups, and executive readouts — distilling complex technical and regulatory issues into clear decisions and actions.
Produce high-quality written communications including project charters, executive briefings, business cases, and post-implementation reviews.
Act as the primary point of contact for third-party payment partners and vendors during integration and certification phases.

Process Improvement & Governance

Define and continuously improve PMO standards, playbooks, and governance frameworks specific to payments programs.
Conduct post-mortem reviews and embed lessons learned into future project planning and team capability building.
Support the development of junior project managers through mentorship, coaching, and structured knowledge sharing.

Strong understanding of project lifecycle methodologies (e.g., Waterfall, Iterative, Agile/Scrum) and project management processes and standards

Excellent verbal and written communications skills; ability to explain project risks and issues, and IT related concepts clearly and concisely to multiple layers of peers and leadership

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst for Lab Production Support, Extended-Hours Support (ExHS)
jobs.description:
Important: this position will work on the Weekend Shift team, with the following rotation schedules:

Tuesday-to-Saturday (including Tue, Wed, Thur, Fri, and Sat), 9AM-to-5PM.
Sunday-to-Thursday (including Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, and Thur), 9AM-to-5PM.

This position will rotate through the above work schedules quarterly, i.e., work in one rotation schedule for 3 calendar months, and then move to the other rotation schedule for another 3 calendar months.

This is an exciting opportunity in our Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) department at Natera (a global leader in precision medicine and genomics testing), to provide critical data analytics support for our lab production operations. As a Senior Data Analyst for Lab Production Support in our DSPE Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) team, you will work in the Weekend Shift team (following the above two rotation schedules). You will have the opportunity to apply innovative data analytics solutions, directly support the most cutting-edge medical diagnostics and genomics applications, and make real & immediate impact to patients and healthcare providers, by providing timely & accurate data analysis support to Natera's production laboratories, as well as for other key business needs.

Primary Responsibilities

Technical Execution and Infrastructure

Deliver timely data support to Lab Operations teams, unblock production issues, and improve patient results turnaround times.
Apply statistical techniques to analyze complex datasets, diagnose operational issues, and support data-driven decision-making.
Perform exploratory data analysis, identify trends, and work with stakeholders to interpret findings and drive continuous improvement.
Design and implement automated solutions for recurring data analysis and production support workflows, improving operational efficiency and scalability.
Extract, transform, and analyze data to generate actionable insights that support lab production operations and business decisions.
Document analytical processes, best practices, and insights to ensure consistency and knowledge transfer across teams.

Process Improvement

Develop and optimize solutions for efficient data retrieval and scalable performance on large and/or complex datasets.
Learn and acquire operational efficiencies on new technologies and solutions developed by other DSPE teams.
Train and coach junior team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Lab Operations and Product teams to identify process issues, assist with root cause analysis, and provide product support.
Represent the Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) team in stakeholder meetings.
Effectively and correctly escalate encountered issues to other DSPE teams.

Qualifications

Masters degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Operational Research, or other related fields.
Minimum 3 years of relevant industry experience.
Minimum 3 years of experience working in a highly regulated environment (e.g., CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings).
Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in data analysis, extraction, querying in production support roles.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Working knowledge of the business processes and requirements of diagnostic laboratories. Knowledge of molecular biology, genetics, genomics, and/or bioinformatics is a plus.
Proficient in data analysis and statistical techniques.
Proficient in Python and SQL development.
Working knowledge of Snowflake platform and cloud technologies.
Strong understanding of statistical concepts such as hypothesis testing, central limit theorem, time series analysis, anomaly detection, and regression modeling.
Good documentation practices and coding style.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience using version control systems such as GitHub or GitLab for managing code and collaboration.
Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment.
Strong interpersonal skills.
Strong integrity.

The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations.

Remote USA

$130,000—$155,000 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

Excelerate LLC is a boutique consulting firm distinguished by its hands-on, collaborative approach to solving complex business challenges. We partner closely with our clients, bringing deeply experienced consultants who work in a facilitative style to deliver practical, lasting impact. Our work is grounded in four core values: humility, energy, integrity, and flexibility. These principles shape our culture, guide our work, and define the people who thrive here.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to drive execution across a portfolio of enterprise transformation initiatives spanning ERP/EPM modernization, Chart of Accounts redesign, contract lifecycle management, and privacy programs. This is a technically fluent leadership role, partnering closely with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to translate complex domain requirements into structured, delivered outcomes.

This role is not about managing status reports – it's about redefining how finance, legal, and privacy operate in a modern, cloud-native environment, and then making it happen.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership

Lead large-scale finance transformation programs (must have led at least two end-to-end transformations).
Coordinate across finance, product, and technology teams to drive execution against roadmap, milestones, and dependencies.
Manage program risks, timelines, and stakeholder alignment in a complex, matrixed environment.
Facilitate executive-level decision-making and provide clear recommendations to senior leadership.

EPM/ERP Domain Expertise & Advisory

Drive key architecture and design decisions across ERP and EPM platforms (Oracle preferred).
Lead evaluation of solution options and tradeoffs, ensuring alignment with long-term business objectives.
Advise on ERP/EPM integration strategy, including how upstream design decisions impact downstream planning and reporting.
Help the SteerCo think through what to automate, what to rethink, and how to move from legacy processes to cloud-native best practices.

Finance Process & Chart of Accounts (CoA) Transformation

Lead redesign of planning, forecasting, and reporting processes, reimagining FP&A for a cloud-native environment.
Enable a modern FP&A operating model that improves cycle times, data accuracy, and decision support.
Lead and advise on end-to-end Chart of Accounts redesign, a core pillar of the transformation.
Ensure alignment between CoA design, EPM planning models, reporting hierarchies, and business dimensions.
Partner with finance stakeholders to align solutions with operational and strategic objectives.

Requirements

Deep expertise in finance process and operating model transformation, with a strong understanding of how to reimagine finance functions (FP&A, Record-to-Report, planning, and reporting) in a cloud-native environment.
Strong understanding of the EPM landscape, including how planning, forecasting, and reporting integrate across platforms.
Experience leading Chart of Accounts redesign and understanding how upstream ERP architecture supports downstream EPM and reporting.
Experience establishing program governance, operating rhythms, and mobilization plans for large-scale transformations.
Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to influence and present to C-suite stakeholders.
Ability to manage ambiguity, competing priorities, and evolving scope in long-term transformation programs.
Bachelor's degree required; MBA or advanced degree in Finance, Technology, or related field preferred.
Comfortable engaging with IST time zone on occasion to support global program coordination.

West Coast candidates considered with occasional travel to Mountain View

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Deputy Project Manager
for a rail transportation project in the New York City
region.

The Deputy Project Manager supports the Project Manager in the day‑to‑day technical, commercial, and coordination activities required to successfully deliver a complex design‑build transportation project. This role acts as a key integrator between engineering disciplines, construction, testing & commissioning, safety, quality, and the client, ensuring that scope, schedule, cost, and contractual obligations are met throughout the project lifecycle.

Your Impact

Key Responsibilities

Project Management & Coordination

Support the Project Manager in overall project execution, planning, and reporting across design, installation, testing, and commissioning phases.
Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams (signaling, communications, track, traction power, systems engineering) to confirm alignment with contract scope and interfaces.
Track progress against schedule and milestones, identify risks and issues, and support mitigation planning.
Prepare inputs for internal and client progress meetings, dashboards, and executive reviews.

Project Controls & Performance Monitoring

Schedule control and progress measurement
Cost tracking, forecasting, and burn rate monitoring
KPI development and performance oversight

Review and challenge Design‑Builder schedule updates, productivity assumptions, and recovery plans.
Support earned value / progress measurement where applicable.
Track early warning indicators to proactively identify delays or cost risks (aligned with PMC performance oversight expectations

Support systems engineering activities, including requirements management, design reviews, and technical stage gate readiness.
Confirm design deliverables are consistent with contract requirements, applicable standards, and approved concepts of operations.
Assist in managing technical interfaces between subsystems and external stakeholders.

Support planning and execution of installation, testing, cutover, and commissioning activities, including review of procedures and reports.
Track and help resolve field issues, NCRs, and technical clarifications in coordination with engineering and quality teams.

Commercial & Contract Management
